newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares start sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: French shares start sharply higher.

text.p: French shares opened sharply higher on Monday on the back of a turnaround on Wall Street and a firmer dollar, dealers said.
The blue chip CAC-40 index opened 1.55 percent higher.
At 0803 GMT, it was up 37.68 points, or 1.5 percent, at 2,555.65. April futures were up 39 points at 2,555 after breaking resistance at 2,550.
Traders said the next objective for the futures contract was 2,600.
"We've had quite a bit of consolidation after the rise in U.S. interest rates and now we are going to rise in line with the dollar's recovery," a broker said.
Brokers said the Noordwijk informal meeting of finance ministers on European Monetary Union had also been positive.
"The market is now convinced that the Euro will be put in place on the scheduled date. That's a lot of uncertainty right out the door," a broker said.
Important data due this week are the German unemployment figures on Tuesday, U.S. jobless claims on Thursday. March retail sales and producer prices are due on Friday.

In France, the Bank of France monetary council will meet on Thursday and the March consumer price index is due on Friday. French June bond futures were also up on Monday morning while the franc was stable.
On the corporate front, most full year results have now been published, with TF1 due for Thursday, and the first quarterly figures are due in coming weeks.

The main focus is on the proposed merger between Lyonnaise des Eaux and Cie de Suez, which will hold special board meetings on Friday to discuss the details of the deal which has been agreed in principle.
Lyonnaise was up 2.44 percent at 546 francs and Suez was two percent higher at 285.60. Le Monde said on Friday that the terms would be 41 Suez shares for 20 Lyonnaise.
